catalog_quote: OPOSIÇÃO POR POSIÇÃO ACENTUAL: DE OXÍTONA PARA PAROXÍTONA. Outra forma de registro encontrada foi a de oposição por marcação acentual: diferença entre as mesmas palavras com acento oxítono para palavras com acento paroxítono. Vejamos: Aiá Feitiço / Áia Sogra / Amá Pisar / Áma Flauta / Caá Andar / Cáa Viajar [...] (p.11). O diacrítico usado para marcar o acento agudo ocorreu em todas as vogais. Esse fato deixa claro que o diacrítico foi usado para marcar a proeminência acentual da palavra. [...] Ou seja, a proeminência acentual pode variar, tanto final de palavras quanto em posição pré-final. Seria o caso de um estudo específico para hipotetizar o comportamento do padrão acentual no Karipuna e quais os condicionantes para essas variações. (p.21)

new_statements.translation: Opposition by accent position: oxytone vs paroxytone. Another kind of record found was opposition by accent marking: a difference between the same words with final (oxytone) accent versus penultimate (paroxytone) accent: Aiá 'sorcery' / Áia 'mother-in-law', Amá 'to step' / Áma 'flute', Caá 'to walk' / Cáa 'to travel' [...]. The acute diacritic occurred on all vowels, which makes clear it was used to mark the accentual prominence of the word. [...] That is, accentual prominence can vary, both word-final and in pre-final position. A specific study would be needed to hypothesize the behaviour of the accentual pattern in Karipuna and the conditioning factors of these variations.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File held by the project (36-page PDF, extracted text has a text layer); UFAC landing page art. 5705 answers 200; CORE also indexes it (core.ac.uk/download/). PDF p. 11: header 'OPOSIÇÃO POR POSIÇÃO ACENTUAL: DE OXÍTONA PARA PAROXÍTONA', 'Outra forma de registro encontrada foi a de oposição por marcação acentual: diferença entre as mesmas palavras com acento oxítono para palavras com acento paroxítono. Vejamos:' Tabela 03 Aiá Feitiço / Áia Sogra / Amá Pisar / Áma Flauta / Caá Andar / Cáa Viajar / Çaú.. Úia Falar — verbatim. PDF p. 21: 'O diacrítico usado para marcar o acento agudo ocorreu em todas as vogais. Esse fato deixa claro que o diacrítico foi usado para marcar a proeminência acentua…
new_statements.relation_note: From Faria's 1927 transcription (Rondon & Faria 1948) the authors read the acute/breve diacritics as marks of word prominence, list about 15 pairs distinguished only by final vs penultimate accent, note disyllables with the 'strong and long' mark are final-stressed, and conclude prominence falls on the final or the penult without a determinable rule; Martius's acutes likewise read as prominence marks (p. 35). No tone claim; nasality and possible length ('Amá/Amáa') discussed.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word prominence (as recorded by Faria 1927 and Martius 1863) falls on the final or the penultimate syllable; position is not predictable from the data and apparently distinguishes lexical pairs (Aiá vs Áia etc.); authors decline to state a rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Authors flag that double vowels may mark length or hiatus rather than stress (Çaú = ça.ú 'jaboti'), and that homographs with identical accent also occur (Çáu 'clavícula/genro/osso'); the whole analysis is an interpretation of 1863/1927 orthographies, explicitly provisional.
new_statements.identity_note: Explicitly the Panoan Karipuna of the Madeira (Martius/Natterer 'Jaun-avo' list and Faria's 1927 E'loé list in Rondon & Faria 1948), compared with Huni Kuin and Kaxarari; secondhand philological analysis, no new field data. File was already in the held dir from a 2026-09-19 lexical pass but is not in the ITEM bibliography and had not been read for prosody.

sources.note: No Caripuna-specific statement. Portuguese-Caripuna wordlist (ca. 500 items, collected 24 Jan 1927 from Vicente Bocamuller) written with Portuguese-style graphic accents (Mapú, Haná, Çumá, Náme, Pôihí). The editors' general note IV (p. 12, PDF p. 12) says only that accent marks on vowels in some vocabularies 'corresponde aos sons fortes e longos de sílabas tônicas' — an orthographic convention for the whole Glossário, not a stress rule.

sources.note: The 'phonological notes' announced by Fleck 2013 are a pronunciation key to Hanke's practical alphabet: vowel and consonant values, diphthongs, nasal vowels (tilde), devoiced 'mute' vowels/consonants written in parentheses (wu(e) 'vento', h(e)nné 'água', shimpa(d) 'peito'), and the convention that stressed ('acentuadas') vowels carry an acute.
